key_insight: Bi-directional Perceptual Shaping (BiPS) converts question-conditioned masked image views into bidirectional where-to-look signals that focus reasoning on fine-grained visual evidence (e.g., chart polylines) while reducing unnecessary visual processing.
problem_solved: Existing VLM reasoning either misses fine-grained visual cues, generalizes poorly across domains, or adds high inference-time cost; BiPS addresses all three by selectively shaping perceptual input to emphasize relevant visual details.
method: Generate question-conditioned masked views of the input image to hide irrelevant regions and emphasize candidate evidence.
Produce bidirectional where-to-look signals (visual guidance in both image→reasoning and reasoning→image directions) to steer token extraction and multimodal reasoning toward fine-grained features.
Integrate the perceptual shaping as a lightweight module or latent-token conditioning step to improve accuracy while keeping inference cost low.
impact: BiPS enables more accurate, efficient multimodal reasoning by capturing fine-grained visual evidence and improving cross-domain generalization — useful for chart understanding, visual question answering, and other VLM applications where detail matters.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image + question → masked views → bidirectional where-to-look maps → VLM reasoning → answer
Before/after comparison: model attention heatmaps showing missed vs. recovered fine-grained cues (e.g., polylines on charts)
Chart plotting trade-off: accuracy vs. inference cost comparing baseline VLMs and BiPS-enabled model
Icon set: masked view, bidirectional arrows (two-way attention), speed/efficiency gauge
paper_title: See Less, See Right: Bi-directional Perceptual Shaping For Multimodal Reasoning
paper_authors: Shuoshuo Zhang, Yizhen Zhang, Jingjing Fu, Lei Song, Jiang Bian
